obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic personal information (name with Social Security, passport, or financial account number, biometric data, or geolocation, among other elements) of individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (a 15-day extension is available for good cause provided in writing to the Department within 30 days)
notify: Each affected individual in Florida, by mail or email; notice gives the date or date range, the information involved, and a company contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - workers, staff, growers who are individuals, and about 9,000 online customers in Florida
clock_starts: Date of determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: HR Director (workers); Vice President of Grower Services (growers); Director of Sales (customers); with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals, never to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with a synopsis, the number of Floridians affected, services offered, a copy of the notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Floridians are affected (likely in the ransomware scenario)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 are notified at once
clock_starts: When the company identifies that more than 1,000 notices are due

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept for at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel decides; company policy is not to rely on it when government identifiers or bank account numbers were taken with names

obligation: Law enforcement delay of individual notice
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in its written request (it may revoke or extend in writing)
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested in writing

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system kept by a third-party agent (payroll provider, HR SaaS, e-commerce vendor, FMIS vendor where it holds personal information)
deadline: Agent must notify the company as expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after its determination; the company then gives the notices above
notify: The company (Security Manager registered as breach contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track for each agent

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected online customers and former workers who live outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents, and state attorneys general or regulators where the state requires it, under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Always check the state of residence of every affected person

obligation: Notice to H-2A workers at home-country addresses (company policy)
citation: Company policy (POL-03 4.7); 20 CFR 655.122(j)(1) requires the home-country address on file
trigger: Personal information of H-2A workers who have returned home is involved
deadline: Same time as the Florida notices
notify: Each affected worker in Spanish by mail, email, and through the H-2A filing agent
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a U.S. state law duty

obligation: H-2A earnings statements and records during an outage (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: Payroll, timekeeping, or field tally unavailable during an incident
deadline: Earnings statement on or before each payday; centrally kept records available within 72 hours of notice from DOL
notify: Each H-2A worker (statement); Department of Labor (on request)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - up to 370 H-2A workers in season

obligation: Produce Safety records on FDA request during an outage (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: FDA requests records while SYS-01 or a site network is unavailable
deadline: Readily available; 24 hours for records kept offsite
notify: FDA (on request)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered farm
owner: Director of Food Safety and Quality

obligation: Food Traceability Rule records on FDA request (readiness)
trigger: FDA requests traceability records to address a threat to public health (for example a recall)
deadline: Within 24 hours of the request, as an electronic sortable spreadsheet for 1.1325-1.1350 records
notify: FDA (on request)
applies_at_this_tier: Readiness only - FDA proposed a 2028-07-20 compliance date (90 FR 38084) and Pub. L. 119-37 sec. 780 directs no enforcement before then
owner: Director of Food Safety and Quality

obligation: Pesticide application and hazard information display (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: SYS-01 unavailable when an application ends
deadline: Display no later than 24 hours after the end of the application
notify: Workers and handlers (central display at each farm)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - agricultural employer

obligation: Application and hazard information to treating medical personnel
trigger: Treating medical personnel request information to inform diagnosis or treatment of a worker or handler
deadline: Promptly after the request
notify: Treating medical personnel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies in an OT integrity event with suspected chemical exposure
owner: HR Director with the Food Safety Coordinator

obligation: FDA notice of a firm-initiated recall (requested)
trigger: The company decides to remove or correct distributed product it believes violative (for example after an OT integrity event)
deadline: FDA requests immediate notice to the appropriate FDA office
notify: FDA, with product identity, reason, risk evaluation, quantities, distribution, recall communication, strategy, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the company initiates a recall (requested, not a fixed statutory deadline)
owner: CEO and Director of Food Safety and Quality, with counsel

obligation: Reportable Food Registry
trigger: Determination that an article of food is a reportable food
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 24 hours after determination
notify: FDA (Reportable Food Registry portal)
applies_at_this_tier: No for the company - the duty is on a responsible party, the person who registers a food facility (350f(a)(1)); the company registers none. Give customers the lot information at once so registered facilities can assess their own duty
owner: Director of Food Safety and Quality

obligation: Retail customer notice of events affecting food safety, traceability, or volumes
trigger: Any event that could affect product safety, lot traceability, or committed volumes (ransomware outage; OT integrity event)
deadline: Within 24 hours of the company becoming aware (contract term)
notify: Each affected retail customer's food safety and category contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
owner: Director of Food Safety and Quality with the Director of Sales

obligation: Contract grower notice
trigger: Incident affecting grower data, the grower portal, or settlement dates
deadline: Within 72 hours of awareness for grower data; before the missed settlement date for payment delays (contract terms)
notify: Each affected contract grower; the growers' association
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Lender and PE sponsor notice
trigger: Severity 1 incident or material disruption
deadline: Per the credit agreement; the sponsor's operating partner is informed by the CEO the same day
notify: Lenders' agent; PE sponsor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging any incident response vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Card processor or acquirer notice
citation: Merchant agreement (contract); Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1.1
trigger: Suspected compromise of the on-farm market terminals or the online store's payment page
deadline: Per merchant agreement (time not set in this sample). Whatever the agreement says, Visa's rules require the compromise to be reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation, through the processor (What To Do If Compromised v10.0, A.1.1)
notify: Card processor; e-commerce vendor
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data or terminals are involved; card data does not enter company systems
verified: n/a (contract term not set); true (Visa clock)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). As proposed, the company would be covered because it exceeds the SBA size standard for NAICS 111998; recheck at each exercise
clock_starts: Proposed: reasonable belief that a covered incident occurred; payment

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI (IC3 or field office); CISA reporting
trigger: Ransomware, extortion, or suspected OT tampering
deadline: As soon as practical (Day 0-2 in the runbooks)
notify: FBI; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; supports the investigation and the OFAC mitigation factors

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability
owner: CEO with counsel and the insurer

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts (the NRCS agreement is a cost-share agreement)

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held
